claims.statement: Each feature module lives under src/modules/<module>/ with convention-based files (index.ts metadata, acl.ts features, setup.ts tenant init, events.ts, di.ts, ce.ts, search.ts, data/entities.ts, data/migrations, api/, backend/, frontend/, subscribers/, workers/, widgets/, i18n/) that the code generator auto-discovers into generated registries.

Auto-discovery file names, expected export names, and directory-to-route mappings (frontend/<path>.tsx -> /<path>, backend/<path>.tsx -> /backend/<path>, api/<method>/<path>.ts -> /api/<path> by method, subscribers/*.ts, workers/*.ts) are a frozen public contract in BACKWARD_COMPATIBILITY.md; existing convention files MUST NOT change in a breaking way, only additive new ones may be added.

apps/mercato/src/modules.ts is the central enablement+override layer: enabledModules lists { id, from, overrides? } entries; official modules are appended from official-modules entries; example_customers_sync is pulled in only when example is enabled; storage_s3 and enterprise modules (record_locks, system_status_overlays, sso, security) are gated by OM_ENABLE_* env flags.

The bundled example module is disabled by default (its enabledModules entry is commented out) and demonstrates the full entry.overrides surface (routes, widgets, events, workers, ACL, DI, encryption, nav); re-enabling it also pulls in the companion example_customers_sync module.

createRequestContainer() builds a per-request Awilix container in InjectionMode.CLASSIC: core engines (em fork, queryEngine, dataEngine, commandRegistry, commandBus, default optimistic-lock guards) first, then module DI registrars (fail-open, logged), then core bootstrap (or replayed cache when OM_BOOTSTRAP_CACHE=1), then the app-level DI registrar, then applyDiOverridesToContainer, then re-registers the tenant encryption subscriber on the fresh EM.

Awilix InjectionMode.CLASSIC resolves factory dependencies by parameter name and passes them positionally, so destructuring patterns like asFunction(({ em }) => ...) silently inject undefined; registrars must use plain named parameters (asFunction((em) => ...)) or chain .proxy().

DI registrars, the cache singleton, the rate limiter, the bootstrap cache, and nav-group ordering state live on globalThis so they survive tsx/esbuild/webpack module duplication and HMR; HMR clears the bootstrap cache so module subscribers can change.

bootstrap() (packages/core/src/bootstrap.ts) wires process-scoped infrastructure into the request container: a singleton cache service (OM_CACHE_SINGLETON, default ON, with memory fallback and SIGTERM/SIGINT close), the event bus (QUEUE_STRATEGY/EVENTS_STRATEGY async|redis|local with no-op fallback that omits dispatchQueued so failures are loud), module subscriber + sync-subscriber registration, KMS + TenantDataEncryptionService (only registers the encryption subscriber when KMS is healthy), a singleton rate limiter (getCachedRateLimiterService never throws), and search module registration (registerSearchModule + search-delete subscriber).

The Phase 5 bootstrap cache (OM_BOOTSTRAP_CACHE=1, default OFF) caches the harvested bootstrap services on globalThis after the first successful bootstrap so later request containers skip the await bootstrap() body and re-register cached instances; it is OFF by default because some bootstrap services close over per-request state (e.g. tenantEncryptionService captures the first request's em fork).

The app-level DI registrar (registerAppDiRegistrar, with a legacy import('@/di') fallback for apps without explicit wiring) runs after core bootstrap and module registrars; the scaffolded app's src/di.ts guards against duplicate bootstrap (skips when eventBus is already registered) and emits application lifecycle events (bootstrapStarted/Completed/Failed).

Three Next.js catch-all dispatchers (api/[...slug]/route.ts, (backend)/backend/[...slug]/page.tsx, (frontend)/[...slug]/page.tsx) import a generated route manifest, match by specificity-sorted patterns, and centrally enforce auth, wildcard-aware RBAC feature checks, tenant selection (enforceTenantSelection, superadmins cross-tenant), organization scope resolution, and rate limiting.

requireRoles route guards are deprecated and ignored at runtime because role names are mutable/spoofable; route metadata MUST use requireFeatures with immutable acl.ts feature IDs, and the dispatcher warns when it encounters a requireRoles guard.

matchFeature() from @open-mercato/shared/lib/auth/featureMatch implements wildcard matching: '*' matches everything, 'prefix.*' matches all features starting with 'prefix.' and the exact prefix itself, and exact match otherwise; hasAllFeatures requires every required feature to be satisfied by some granted feature. Never use includes()/Set.has()/ad hoc every(...includes(...)) for feature checks.

RBAC features are declared in acl.ts as Array<{id,title,module,dependsOn?}> using the <module>.<action> naming convention, granted to default roles via setup.ts defaultRoleFeatures, and propagated to existing tenants by the idempotent `yarn mercato auth sync-role-acls` command (new tenants get them during setup).

Optimistic locking is ON by default (OM_OPTIMISTIC_LOCK; opt out with off/false/0/no/disabled/none) and relies on an updated_at column; user-editable entities MUST include updated_at and return updatedAt in list/detail responses or CrudForm's auto-derive silently no-ops and concurrent edits are lost, and the optimistic-lock-editable-entities.test.ts guard fails if a curated editable entity drops it. Append-only logs, junction/assignment tables, session/token rows, job rows, and parent-aggregate-guarded sub-resource lines are exempt.

The default OSS optimistic-lock guards (crudMutationGuardService and commandOptimisticLockGuardService) are registered as scoped asFunction in createRequestContainer reading from the global reader store; module di.ts registrations (and the enterprise record_locks module) override these DI keys via Awilix replace semantics to back them with record locks.

MikroORM runs as a process-level singleton (getOrm()); createRequestContainer() forks orm.em with clear:true, freshEventManager:true, useContext:true so request-level subscribers (e.g. encryption) do not pile up globally, giving each request container its own EntityManager fork.

Migrations are generated and applied per-module (files live in src/modules/<module>/migrations/) with no global schema; tables use plural snake_case with <module>_ prefixes, UUID PKs, explicit FKs, and deleted_at for soft delete. Modules MUST NOT create direct ORM relationships across modules — they reference each other by FK IDs + snapshots, verified by the module-decoupling test.

Each process gets its own MikroORM pool (DB_POOL_MAX default 20) configured via resolvePoolConfig(); because each background worker job runs in its own request container with one pooled connection, the invariant web_pool_max + worker_pool_max + scheduler/overhead <= Postgres max_connections MUST hold with headroom, and worker job concurrency is bound by OM_WORKERS_DB_CONNECTION_BUDGET (with DB_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_MS/DB_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS tuning).

Encrypted entities MUST be queried via findWithDecryption/findOneWithDecryption/findAndCountWithDecryption from @open-mercato/shared/lib/encryption/find (never raw em.find), always supplying tenantId and organizationId; GDPR-sensitive fields are declared in the module's encryption.ts defaultEncryptionMaps, and encryption maps default to tenant-scoped keys with an additive keyScope:'system' option for pre-tenant records.

Organization scope is resolved per request by resolveOrganizationScopeForRequest (packages/core/src/modules/directory/utils/organizationScope.ts) from cookies + RBAC, with per-request memoization and a short-TTL cache with tag-based invalidation.

When BACKEND_CUSTOM_DOMAINS_ENABLED is on and a hostname resolves to a backend-target DomainMapping, the request Host authoritatively narrows organization scope (it can only narrow, never widen): applySuperAdminScope (packages/shared/src/lib/auth/server.ts) applies the host binding at all three auth call sites (cookie, token, API-key) before the cookie override is written (conflicting cookie discarded, cross-tenant session refused with 403) and adds a hostBinding field to AuthContext, and resolveOrganizationScopeForRequest forces the mapping's org/tenant into effectiveTenantId/normalizedSelectedId and adds the bound org as an explicit cache-key component so a poisoned entry cannot be shared (__all__ on a bound host is a hard 4xx).

The host binding is registered into packages/shared at bootstrap by customer_accounts/di.ts because shared cannot import the module where DomainMapping lives; the feature is gated by BACKEND_CUSTOM_DOMAINS_ENABLED (default off) and hard-fails at boot without TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS since the base compose stack exposes the app port where any client can forge a Host header.

A module di.ts exports register(container) that registers entities as values and services into the Awilix container; it may also register optimistic-lock readers at module-load time via registerOptimisticLockReaders (e.g. customers registers readers for both 'customers.person' and 'customers.people' resource kinds because the factory does not singularize the irregular plural 'people').

entry.overrides is the ONLY canonical override surface (never patch upstream module source): applyModuleOverridesFromEnabledModules dispatches every overrides.<domain> shape to wired appliers (api/pages routes, subscribers, workers, widgets, notifications, interceptors, enrichers, guards, cli, setup, acl, encryption, di, nav); API-route keys are 'METHOD /api/path' (method case-insensitive, leading slash optional, trailing slashes stripped), page keys are '/backend/path' or '/frontend/path', null disables a method, and {handler,metadata?} replaces it.

setup.ts (ModuleSetupConfig) declares tenant lifecycle hooks: onTenantCreated (settings rows, sequences — always, idempotent), seedDefaults (dictionaries, tax rates, statuses — always during init/onboarding), seedExamples (demo data — skipped with --no-examples), and defaultRoleFeatures (declarative, merged during ensureDefaultRoleAcls() and sync-role-acls); modules MUST NOT hardcode setup logic in setup-app.ts or directly import another module's seed functions.

Server authorization uses the consolidated feature policy (authorizeFeatures/resolveEffectiveFeatures from @open-mercato/shared/security/featurePolicy) or the realm services (rbacService.userHasAllFeatures / customerRbacService.userHasAllFeatures); policy ordering denies invalid scope and nulled/disabled features before super-admin or wildcard grants, isSuperAdmin grants all active features, and resolveEffectiveFeatures returns concrete IDs (never wildcards) for browser capability payloads.

The module-decoupling test (packages/core/src/__tests__/module-decoupling.test.ts) verifies the app works when optional modules are disabled by registering only a subset of modules via registerModules(); cross-module optional integration must use a per-module tryResolve helper wrapping container.resolve() that returns undefined when the peer is absent, then no-op or degrade — never declare a hard requires on an optional peer.

makeCrudRoute() (@open-mercato/shared/lib/crud/factory.ts) handles Zod validation, RBAC feature gating (requiredFeatures), CRUD list/detail/create/update/delete, custom fields, optimistic locking, response enrichers, API interceptors, mutation guards, multi-id (?ids=) filtering, list caching, exporters, and sync event emission; custom non-CRUD write routes MUST wire runMutationGuards(...) from the mutation-guard-registry before mutation logic.

Every auto-discovery file convention, public type, and function signature in BACKWARD_COMPATIBILITY.md is a public contract; changes MUST follow the deprecation protocol (deprecate first with @deprecated + migration guidance, provide a bridge, document in UPGRADE_NOTES.md, reference a spec with a Migration & Backward Compatibility section) or they are breaking changes that block merge, with a narrow emergency security exception that waives only steps 1-3 when the surface being removed is itself the vulnerability.
